title: I Need Time!
reviewNotes: Three branches, 11 exact positions from the visually reconstructed seven-piece phase after ...Rxg1 at 70 seconds. The earlier eight-piece Rg1 sacrifice remains source context. g7 ...Rh1 g8=Q+ ...Kd7 Qxg2 is the illustrated winning race. Independent ...Rf1 is also checked, and independent Ke5 loses at once. Every encoded intermediate position is checked; no exact proof is claimed for the unencoded eight-piece setup.
transcript: Fools will resign. Wise players might make a draw, but only a true genius would be able to win from this position. You see, there's a big problem. Black is only one step away from getting a new queen. And if we try to take this rook, well, now the pawn is not going to promote here. He's going to take our rook and promote like this. And now, even if we try to run with our own pawn, the black queen is simply too fast and black is going to win the game. Trying to stop the pawn like this, of course, doesn't work. Black simply gets a queen for free and we still lose. And giving checks to this king doesn't really lead to anything. We still have the problem of the pawn that is about to promote. [music] So, white has to keep checking this black king. And this [applause] is going to be a draw, but nothing more than that. So, it seems like black is simply out of the woods in this position and white should be content with a draw, right? Well, not exactly, because white has a brilliant resource that will allow him to win this position. And the brilliant, only winning move of white is the incredible and stunning rook to G1. A move that looks like the most outrageous blunder we can play in this position. The rook could simply take us, right? First of all, if the rook doesn't take and, for example, runs back to try and stop this pawn, well, we can simply pick up this and now the pawn is protected and this is going to be an easy win. But after the rook takes, we start to see the brilliant plan of white unfolding. Because, you see, all we needed was to stop this pawn for a couple of moves while we push our own pawn. And now the pawn and king are shouldering the black king. There is no way to come and stop this pawn and black is not free to push his own pawn. So, it will have to try and run with the rook to stop us. But it seems to be too slow. We're going to get a queen with check, win the other pawn and very easily win this game. If you're loving incredible chess, follow for more.
